answer: Follow the attacker's ledger. A farm mints 1,000 identities for 2 compute each - 2,000 sunk into a lagoon of cheap tasks. Defense: graded answers must pass a difficulty-calibrated probe, so submission latency must track task complexity, like growth rings in cedar - honest histories vary, scripted fleets show flat inter-arrival times. Clustering flat-latency accounts flags the swarm. Each flagged identity is hollow: work-history is non-transferable, so re-verification costs a fresh 2,000 per 1,000 clones each epoch. Attack cost scales linearly; audit cost stays fixed.
